result.method:
I wrote my own implementation, using only integers and Fractions in every decision. I did not import ctln, fastregion, region2d, symbolic or anything under n7/. Sympy was used once, only to cross-check one factorisation. Everything ran in one process in about 20 s.

(i) Structure. I wrote my own digraph6 decoder and encoder (they round-trip). For each graph I checked: no loops; arc count matches the record's 'edges'; not complete bidirected, with the number of missing arcs recorded; the 'clique' field. Domination-freeness uses Lemma D / Curto Def 1.1 literally: k dominates j iff j->k, k does not send to j, and every i outside {j,k} with i->j also has i->k. I checked all ordered pairs. Isomorphism uses my own canonical form (lexicographically maximal row-major bit string over all 5040 permutations). nauty n7/labelg gave a second opinion. I matched the 123 'in_limit_candidates' against certificates/COUNTEREXAMPLE_CANDIDATES_n7_limit.jsonl up to isomorphism. I also checked that the limit file's 'A' field equals the decode of its d6, and that the record's 'canonical' d6 is isomorphic to its 'd6'.

(ii) Limit check for the 123. I computed m*chi_perp = chi_A - chi_{A+J} with exact Faddeev-LeVerrier and checked its leading coefficient is m = 7 with integer coefficients. I cross-checked chi_perp a second way: the charpoly of (V^T V)^{-1} V^T A V with V = [e_i - e_7]. The beta used is beta_sample of the first stable cell, which has t_hi = null in all 123 cases. With gamma = 1 - 1/beta, I ran a Hurwitz test on g(x) = chi_perp(x - gamma); a zero minor counts as undecided. I solved w = (A^T + gamma I)^{-1} 1 exactly and checked w > 0. I also checked beta > 2.

Extra checks, independent of Lemma I. At finite parameters I built W from A, eps, delta (with the transpose convention) and asserted I - W = -delta I + (1+delta) J - (eps+delta) A^T entrywise. I solved (I - W) x = 1 exactly and checked x > 0, then ran Hurwitz on det(xI - (-I + W)). These checks used (a) every stable cell's sample point (beta_sample with the t_sample taken from region2d), converted by eps = 1/(t+1), delta = (beta-1) eps, plus a legality check, and (b) all 4 pointwise witnesses per graph in the limit file.

(iii) FNFL. I computed m*chi_perp, divided exactly by l^2+l+1 with my own long division, and ran Hurwitz on the quotient shifted by -1/2. I also checked its two finite witnesses.

FNFL
- m*chi_perp = 7l^6 + 28l^5 + 56l^4 + 68l^3 + 52l^2 + 24l + 5 = (l+1)(l^2+l+1)(7l^3+14l^2+14l+5). My exact division leaves remainder 0; sympy's factor_list agrees.
